label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences (t=5, outputting orig(2))
explanation: Fires almost only at the last copy step of length-3 sequences: t=5, where the input is the echoed second token and the model outputs the third original token. About 85% of steps with L=3, t=5 are active, and they hold 89% of the activation mass. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on a first occurrence of a token. Magnitude depends on the sequence content: the largest activations come from sequences that start with c, q or a (that predicate is 98.5% precise but covers few activations), and sequences with no digits activate more often. Inactive L=3 cases tend to have d, 0, i or a as the second token. The remaining ~11% of mass is a weak tail at late copy steps of longer sequences, mostly the last or second-to-last output (e.g. t=11 for L=6, t=17 for L=9, t=6 for L=4). Adding these clauses lowers precision a lot.

issues: Minor overclaim: the claim that 'sequences with no digits activate more often' barely holds. Precision is 0.854 with no digits vs 0.847 with digits, so the difference is negligible.

Count recall is only 0.66 (1144 missed test steps), but the misses are weak (relative activation about 0.01-0.23) and spread across late copy steps of longer sequences. Tail candidates all score poorly: (L==6)&(t==11) precision 0.016, (L==9)&(t==17) 0.017, in_tok=='b' near the end 0.047, and repeated input near the end 0.018. I found no systematic class of misses that a predicate could capture.

Confirmed: no activity in the original or delimiter phase; 89% of mass at t=5, all of it with L=3; the c/q/a first-token subset is 98.5% precise but covers only 15% of mass; false positives cluster on second tokens d/0/i/a (precision 0.48 vs 0.91 without them), and excluding those tokens lowers F1 (0.732 vs 0.745); every predicate-true step has correct==1.
